title: SRE reliability huddle — pre-sync notes & actions (May 4 2026)
content:
Quick scratchpad for the weekly ops sync + reliability review. Goal: surface surprises, confirm owners for follow-ups, and get agreement on immediate mitigations before next oncall rotation.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m quick SLO snapshot + trend callouts
- 10m paging/noise breakdown (root causes & short fixes)
- 10m top incidents review (what still open, runbook gaps)
- 5m action item assignment + deadlines

SLO snapshot (rolling 30d):
- serving-api availability target: 99.95%
  - current: 99.89% (delta -0.06) — trending down last 7d
  - primary contributor: short spikes causing 5xx for <5m windows across 3 zones
- tokenization-worker latency P95 target: 200ms
  - current P95: 230ms (median stable) — jitter during high-rt batching
- embedding pipeline success rate target: 99.9%
  - current: 99.96% (good)

Paging trends (last 14d):
- total pages up ~18% WoW (from 95 -> 112)
- noise fraction ~42% of pages (alerts that didn't require escalation)
- top noisy alert groups:
  1) redis-conn-fail (alerts on transient connection resets) — spike 4/28 and 5/2 after infra network change
    - hypothesis: orchestration restart order exposed a race that briefly increased connection churn
    - quick mitigation: relax redis-conn alert for <30s flaps (threshold change) + add backoff in client
  2) scheduled-batch-timeout — several 1-2min timeouts when large batches hit constrained GPU nodes
    - short fix: temporary batch size cap per route (limit 1.5x for heavy routes)
  3) gpu-scheduler-oom (low frequency, high severity) — 4/19 incident burned through reserved headroom
    - see incident notes below

Top incidents (summary & open items):
- INC-2026-0419-gpu-scheduler-oom — severity 2
  - summary: unexpected concurrent large-model cold starts caused GPU scheduler to overcommit memory; node-level OOMs and pod restarts for ~22 minutes in us-west-2
  - immediate impact: 6 endpoints elevated latency and ~0.7% availability hit during window
  - root cause (current): heuristics for GPU memory pre-check didn't account for multi-model cache warming (KV cache + model weight paging)
  - runbook gaps: no explicit step for temporarily draining warmup traffic; rollout guidance unclear for mixed-model nodes
  - actions: (A) add heuristic guardrail in scheduler to reserve X% memory for cache warming — owner: Jonas Reed — due: 2026-05-11; (B) create emergency drain play in runbook + test on staging — owner: Maya Singh — due: 2026-05-08

- INC-2026-0428-kvcache-evict-thrash — severity 3
  - summary: KV cache eviction thrash when prefix cache TTLs dropped after one of the config rollouts; caused increase in serving tail latency for small-chat workloads (~P99 spike to 1.2s)
  - immediate impact: customer-reported latency regressions, two oncall pages escalated
  - root cause: config rollout changed default ttl from 5m -> 30s (oops), not caught by canary
  - actions: (A) revert config rollout back to 5m default — owner: Ethan Park — done: 2026-05-04; (B) add pre-rollout smoke test that validates tail latency on critical routes — owner: Ava Martinez — due: 2026-05-12

Open runbook and tooling gaps:
- no clear checklist for capacity-sensitive rollouts that touch both scheduler and cache behavior (high risk)
- alert thresholds for redis client flaps are too aggressive for brief infra-induced resets
- lack of synthetic canaries for mixed-model cold-start behavior — needs a low-cost synthetic profile

Proposed immediate mitigations (fast, low-friction):
- relax redis-conn alert to 30s sliding window and add annotation for infra maintenance windows — owner: Jonas Reed — due: 2026-05-06
- implement temporary batch-size cap per heavy route via runtime config (config flag) — owner: oncall this week (Maya) to flip on if pages continue — escalates to engineering if >3 pages in 24h
- add a one-time postmortem 'quick blameless writeup' for the two incidents to capture timeline and decisions (short doc, link to JIRA) — owner: Ava Martinez — due: 2026-05-07

Follow-ups for next sync (things to report back):
- Jonas: telemetry on redis-conn alert changes (did noise drop?) — bring metric: pages/day for redis-conn alerts
- Ethan: confirm config enforcement added to CI so TTL regresses can't ship unnoticed — show test coverage
- Maya: staged test of emergency drain playbook on staging cluster (results + gaps)
- Ava: draft of 'capacity-aware rollout checklist' and proposed gating in the console (for Dedicated)

Questions / talking points for ops manager and product:
- short-term: can product temporarily gate large model cold-starts to fewer nodes during rollout windows? (helps reduce scheduler OOM risk)
- long-term: what's appetite for adding mixed-model synthetic canaries? cost vs benefit?

Parking lot (not for this sync):
- longer-term research into KV cache eviction policies (LRU vs size-aware) and impact on tail latency
- investigate autoscaler behavior under 'mixed heat' workloads to avoid scheduling surprises

Quick TODO table (capture here to avoid forgetting in sync):
- [ ] Jonas: change redis alert thresholds (due 2026-05-06)
- [x] Ethan: revert kvcache TTL config (done 2026-05-04)
- [ ] Maya: implement & test emergency drain runbook (due 2026-05-08)
- [ ] Ava: write quick incident summary doc + create postmortem stub (due 2026-05-07)
- [ ] Ava: propose rollout checklist + Console gating spec (due 2026-05-12)

Notes to self: keep sync tight — focus on 1-2 actions we can actually finish this week. Call out any cross-org blockers early (product, infra). If product wants to push a schedule change, require a one-line risk register entry in PR description.

End of notes. Bring up the batch-size cap as 'surgical' measure rather than wholesale throttling.
